title: Synthesis and crystallographic characterization of diphenylamide rare-earth metal complexes Ln(NPh2)3(THF)2 and [(Ph2N)2Ln(μ-NPh2)]2

synthesis.procedure: Under argon with rigorous exclusion of air and water (Schlenk/glovebox), YCl3 (0.63 g, 3.2 mmol) was stirred for two days in THF (30 mL) in a Schlenk flask. Under N2, KNPh2 (1.9 g, 9.1 mmol) in THF (30 mL) was added dropwise to the YCl3 suspension at 273 K over 15 min. After warming to room temperature for 1 h, solvent was removed under reduced pressure. The product was extracted with toluene, evaporated, and washed with hexane to give colorless 1-Y (2.2 g, 90%). Dissolution in diethyl ether and storage at 245 K for three days yielded colorless crystals.
synthesis.temperature: 273 K addition, then room temperature; crystallization at 245 K
synthesis.time: YCl3 stirred 2 days in THF; 15 min addition; 1 h after warming; crystals after 3 days
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Schlenk flask under N2; glovebox workup
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: solvent removed under reduced pressure; toluene extraction; hexane wash; crystallized from diethyl ether at 245 K

synthesis.procedure: In a glovebox, ErCl3 (243 mg, 0.887 mmol) was stirred in THF (10 mL) to give a pink slurry. NaNPh2 (500 mg, 2.62 mmol) in THF (10 mL) was added dropwise at 238 K over 5 min (color change green–yellow then pink). After warming to room temperature and stirring overnight, volatiles were removed to a pink gel, triturated with hexane, then dissolved in Et2O (17 mL). Unreacted solids were centrifuged off; the supernatant was concentrated to supersaturation. Large pink hexagonal crystals of 1-Er grew as the solution warmed to room temperature (260 mg, 36%).
synthesis.temperature: 238 K addition, then room temperature overnight; crystals on warming to room temperature
synthesis.time: 5 min addition; overnight stirring; crystals within minutes after concentration
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: volatiles removed; hexane trituration; Et2O dissolution; centrifugation; crystallization from concentrated Et2O

synthesis.procedure: In a glovebox free of coordinating solvents, Y[N(SiMe3)2]3 (300 mg, 0.526 mmol) in toluene (10 mL) was treated with HNPh2 (272 mg, 1.61 mmol) in toluene (10 mL) and stirred 48 h (colorless to yellow with yellow precipitate). Volatiles were removed; solids were washed with hexane, stirred in benzene 48 h, and centrifuged. Toluene (4 mL) was added to the supernatant, concentrated to 4 mL, and layered with hexane (15 mL). After 48 h at room temperature, yellow rectangular blocks of 2-Y formed.
synthesis.time: 48 h reaction; 48 h benzene stir; 48 h crystallization
synthesis.vessel_or_method: glovebox free of coordinating solvents; centrifugation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: volatiles removed; hexane wash; benzene extraction/centrifugation; toluene concentrate layered with hexane

synthesis.procedure: In a glovebox free of coordinating solvents, Er[N(SiMe3)2]3 (300 mg, 0.463 mmol) in toluene (10 mL) was treated with HNPh2 (240 mg, 1.41 mmol) in toluene (10 mL) and stirred 48 h (colorless to yellow). Volatiles were removed; yellow solids were washed with hexane, stirred in benzene 48 h, and centrifuged. Toluene (4 mL) was added to the supernatant, concentrated to 4 mL, and layered with hexane (15 mL). After 48 h at room temperature, yellow rectangular blocks of 3-Er formed. The compound is a minor product of formal hydrolysis of 2-Er, presumably from adventitious water.
